questions.question: Why is the focal length of a plane mirror considered to be infinite?
options: A plane mirror has no curvature, so its radius of curvature is infinity
Parallel rays reflected from it cross at zero distance
Plane mirrors cannot form images of distant objects
The mirror completely transmits all incident light
questions.correct_answer: A plane mirror has no curvature, so its radius of curvature is infinity
questions.explanation: Because a plane mirror is completely flat, r = ∞. Since f = r/2, its focal length f is infinity.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the angle of deviation (δ), angle of incidence (i), angle of emergence (e), and angle of prism (A)?
questions.explanation: For refraction through a triangular glass prism, the total deviation angle is given by δ = i + e - A.

questions.question: Why does an optical fiber transmit light signals with virtually no loss of intensity over kilometers?
options: Light undergoes successive total internal reflections where 100% of the energy is reflected
The fiber has electrical amplifiers embedded inside every millimeter
Light converts into electrical voltage inside the core
The fiber core acts as a silvered concave mirror
questions.correct_answer: Light undergoes successive total internal reflections where 100% of the energy is reflected
questions.explanation: In total internal reflection, no light is refracted or absorbed at the ideal boundary, resulting in 100% reflection without loss of light intensity.

questions.question: When an object is placed between the center of curvature and principal focus of a concave mirror, what are the nature and position of the image?
options: Real, inverted, diminished, between C and F
Real, inverted, same size, at C
questions.explanation: For an object between C and F of a concave mirror, the reflected rays converge beyond C, forming a real, inverted, and enlarged image.

questions.question: Why does a pencil dipped obliquely in a beaker of water appear bent at the water surface?
options: Light rays coming from the underwater part of the pencil bend away from the normal upon exiting into air
Water molecules mechanically bend the wood of the pencil
Light is completely absorbed by the surface layer of water
The surface of water behaves like a convex mirror
questions.correct_answer: Light rays coming from the underwater part of the pencil bend away from the normal upon exiting into air
questions.explanation: Light from submerged points refracts away from the normal as it leaves the water, making those points appear raised relative to their true position.

questions.question: What is the nature of the image formed by a concave lens for any real object position?
options: Always real, erect, and same size
Can be real or virtual depending on object distance
questions.explanation: A concave lens diverges all incident light rays, so they always appear to originate from a point between the optical center and focus on the same side, creating an erect, diminished virtual image.

questions.question: How does the speed of a wave change when it passes from deep water into shallow water?
options: Speed decreases while frequency remains unchanged
Speed remains constant while frequency decreases
questions.correct_answer: Speed decreases while frequency remains unchanged
questions.explanation: Frequency is determined solely by the wave source and does not change across media. In shallower water, wave speed decreases, causing wavelength to shorten.

questions.question: Why does an echo sound fainter than the original sound produced?
options: Part of the sound energy is absorbed by the reflecting surface and spreads out spherically
Sound frequency drops below the audible range during reflection
The speed of sound decreases dramatically during reflection
Sound waves lose mass as they travel through air
questions.correct_answer: Part of the sound energy is absorbed by the reflecting surface and spreads out spherically
questions.explanation: A portion of the acoustic wave energy is absorbed by the obstacle and the air, and spherical spreading over distance reduces sound intensity (inverse-square law).

questions.question: What is the function of the ciliary muscles in accommodation of the human eye?
options: They alter the curvature and focal length of the eye lens
They open and close the eyelid
They rotate the eyeball in its socket
They change the color sensitivity of retinal cones
questions.correct_answer: They alter the curvature and focal length of the eye lens
questions.explanation: Ciliary muscles relax to flatten the lens for distant viewing and contract to make the lens thicker and more convex for focusing on near objects.

questions.question: Why does the diamond sparkle so brilliantly compared to an ordinary piece of cut glass?
options: Diamond has a very high refractive index (2.42) and a very small critical angle (~24.4°)
Diamond is inherently radioactive and emits its own light
Diamond absorbs all colors of light except white
Diamond has a negative refractive index
questions.correct_answer: Diamond has a very high refractive index (2.42) and a very small critical angle (~24.4°)
questions.explanation: A tiny critical angle of 24.4° ensures that almost any light entering a properly cut diamond suffers multiple total internal reflections before exiting through the top facets.

questions.question: If a concave mirror has an object placed at its center of curvature (C), what is the linear magnification?
questions.explanation: When the object is at C, the image also forms at C with equal height but inverted, giving m = -v/u = -(-2f)/(-2f) = -1.

questions.question: Why is red light used for danger signals on roads, towers, and railways?
options: Red light has the longest wavelength in visible light and scatters least in fog and smoke
Red light travels twice as fast as blue light in air
Red light has the highest frequency of all colors
questions.correct_answer: Red light has the longest wavelength in visible light and scatters least in fog and smoke
questions.explanation: By Rayleigh scattering (scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴), red light's longer wavelength minimizes scattering by airborne dust and water droplets, allowing it to be seen over greatest distances.

questions.question: What is the relationship between power of combination of two thin lenses in contact, P1 and P2?
questions.explanation: When thin lenses are held in close contact, their net focal length is 1/f = 1/f1 + 1/f2, which directly means net power P = P1 + P2.

questions.question: A sound wave has a frequency of 500 Hz and travels at 340 m/s. What is its wavelength?
A radio transmitter broadcasts at a frequency of 100 MHz. What is the wavelength of the radio wave in vacuum? (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
A tuning fork vibrates 256 times in one second. What is its period of oscillation?
A person claps their hands near a tall cliff and hears the echo 1.2 seconds later. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, how far is the cliff?
questions.explanation: Sound travels to the cliff and back: 2d = v × t → d = (340 × 1.2) / 2 = 408 / 2 = 204 m.

questions.question: A ship's sonar emits an ultrasound pulse into the ocean and receives the reflected signal after 2.0 seconds. If sound travels at 1500 m/s in seawater, what is the water depth?
A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 40 cm. What is its focal length?
questions.explanation: Focal length f = r / 2 = 40 cm / 2 = 20 cm.

questions.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Where is the image formed?
options: At 30 cm in front of the mirror
At 10 cm in front of the mirror
questions.correct_answer: At 30 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: Here u = -30 cm and f = -15 cm (object is at center of curvature C = 2f). The image forms at C: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = -1/15 - (-1/30) = -1/30 → v = -30 cm (30 cm in front).

questions.question: An object 4 cm tall is placed in front of a concave mirror, producing an inverted image 8 cm tall. What is the linear magnification?
questions.explanation: Magnification m = height of image / height of object = -8 cm / 4 cm = -2 (negative indicates inverted image).

questions.question: Light travels from air into a transparent medium at an angle of incidence of 45°, and refracts at an angle of 30°. What is the refractive index of the medium?
The speed of light in vacuum is 3 × 10⁸ m/s. What is the speed of light in a glass block with refractive index 1.5?
What is the power of a convex lens with a focal length of +0.25 m?
A person wears eyeglasses with a power of -2.0 D. What type of lens is it and what is its focal length?
options: Concave lens with focal length -0.5 m
Convex lens with focal length +0.5 m
Concave lens with focal length -2.0 m
Convex lens with focal length +2.0 m
questions.correct_answer: Concave lens with focal length -0.5 m
questions.explanation: Negative power means a diverging (concave) lens. f = 1 / P = 1 / (-2.0 D) = -0.5 m (-50 cm).

questions.question: A water tank is 4.0 meters deep. What is its apparent depth when viewed normally from above? (Refractive index of water = 4/3)
questions.explanation: Apparent depth = real depth / n = 4.0 m / (4/3) = 3.0 m.

questions.question: A sound wave of frequency 680 Hz travels at 340 m/s. What is the phase difference between two points separated by 0.25 m along the wave path?
questions.explanation: λ = v / f = 340 / 680 = 0.5 m. Phase difference Δφ = (2π / λ) × Δx = (2π / 0.5) × 0.25 = π radians (180°).

questions.question: Two thin lenses of powers +3.5 D and -1.5 D are placed in contact. What is the focal length of the combination?
questions.explanation: Net power P = P1 + P2 = +3.5 + (-1.5) = +2.0 D. Net focal length f = 1 / P = 1 / 2.0 = +0.5 m (50 cm).

questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm produces a real image at a distance of 60 cm on the other side. What was the object distance?
If the critical angle for a glass-air boundary is 42°, what is the refractive index of the glass? (sin 42° ≈ 0.669)
A person stands 1.5 m in front of a flat wall mirror. What is the distance between the person and their image?
questions.explanation: In a plane mirror, image distance behind the mirror equals object distance in front (1.5 m). Total distance from person to image = 1.5 m + 1.5 m = 3.0 m.

questions.question: If you walk towards a plane mirror at a speed of 1.2 m/s, at what speed does your image approach you?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = speed of person + speed of image relative to mirror = 1.2 m/s + 1.2 m/s = 2.4 m/s.

questions.question: A sound wave travels in water at 1480 m/s with a wavelength of 0.74 m. What is its frequency?
A student standing between two parallel walls claps once. He hears the first echo after 0.4 s and the second echo after 0.6 s. What is the distance between the two walls? (Speed of sound = 340 m/s)
A ray of light reflects from a plane mirror. If the angle between the incident ray and reflected ray is 80°, what is the angle of incidence?
questions.explanation: Angle between incident and reflected rays is i + r = 2i (since i = r). So 2i = 80° → i = 40°.

questions.question: If a plane mirror is rotated by an angle of 15°, through what angle does the reflected ray turn?
questions.explanation: When a mirror is rotated through angle θ keeping the incident ray fixed, the reflected ray rotates by 2θ = 2 × 15° = 30°.

questions.question: An object 2 cm high is placed 10 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. What is the nature and size of the image?
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/15 + (-1/10) = -1/30 → v = -30 cm (virtual, behind object). Magnification m = v/u = (-30)/(-10) = +3. Image height = 3 × 2 cm = 6 cm erect.

questions.question: What is the speed of light in water if the refractive index of water is 1.33? (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
A concave shaving mirror has a radius of curvature of 50 cm. To see an upright, enlarged face, within what distance from the mirror must the user stand?
questions.explanation: f = r/2 = 25 cm. To form an upright, magnified virtual image in a concave mirror, the object must be between the pole and focus (u < 25 cm).

questions.question: A sound wave has a wavelength of 0.2 m in air where speed is 340 m/s. When this sound enters water (speed = 1500 m/s), what will its new wavelength be?
questions.explanation: Frequency f = v_air / λ_air = 340 / 0.2 = 1700 Hz (constant). λ_water = v_water / f = 1500 / 1700 ≈ 0.88 m.

questions.question: A person cannot see objects clearly beyond 80 cm. What lens power is needed to enable normal distant vision?
questions.explanation: For myopia with far point d = 80 cm (0.8 m), the corrective concave lens must have focal length f = -0.8 m. Power P = 1/f = 1 / (-0.8) = -1.25 D.

questions.question: A hypermetropic person has a near point of 75 cm. What lens power is required to read a book comfortably at 25 cm?
questions.explanation: Object distance u = -25 cm = -0.25 m; virtual image at near point v = -75 cm = -0.75 m. 1/f = 1/v - 1/u = -1/0.75 - (-1/0.25) = -1.333 + 4.0 = +2.67 D.

questions.question: A vibrating blade completes 120 cycles in 3 seconds. What is the frequency of its sound?
questions.explanation: Frequency f = total cycles / total time = 120 / 3 s = 40 Hz.

questions.question: An ultrasound scanner operates at 2.5 MHz in human soft tissue where acoustic velocity is 1540 m/s. What is the ultrasound wavelength?
A convex mirror on a bus has a radius of curvature of 2.0 m. If a car is 5.0 m behind the mirror, what is the image distance?
What is the minimum height of a flat vertical mirror required for a 180 cm tall person to view their complete reflection?
questions.explanation: By geometry of similar triangles in reflection, the minimum mirror length to see one's full height is half the person's height: H/2 = 180 / 2 = 90 cm.

questions.question: A light ray strikes a glass plate with an angle of incidence of 60°. If the reflected ray and refracted ray are mutually perpendicular (90° apart), what is the refractive index of glass?
questions.explanation: When reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular, Brewster's condition applies: n = tan(ip) = tan(60°) = √3 ≈ 1.732.

questions.question: A loudspeaker emits sound with an intensity that produces 60 dB at 10 m. If distance from the speaker increases to 20 m, what factor does the sound intensity drop by?
questions.explanation: Sound intensity from a point source follows the inverse square law: I ∝ 1/r². Doubling distance from 10 m to 20 m reduces intensity by (1/2)² = 1/4.

questions.question: A beam of light traveling in water (n = 1.33) encounters an air boundary. What is the critical angle for water?
A projector lens has a focal length of 10 cm and throws a sharp slide image onto a screen 210 cm away. What is the magnification of the image?
